questions.q: Why does the summary compare endings to pruning a rose bush?
a: Cutting back what is unhealthy helps new growth
Both require special tools and expert help
Both are painful and best avoided
Both happen on a fixed yearly schedule
questions.why: Lesson 1 says pruning a rose bush makes it healthier and more colorful, just as endings help your life bloom.

questions.q: What did Jack Welch's cutbacks at GE produce?
a: A rise in market value and a top market position
A smaller company with lower profits
A workforce that resisted all change
A reputation for avoiding hard choices
questions.why: Lesson 1 cites GE's market value rising from 14 billion to 410 billion dollars after Welch's layoffs and cancellations.

questions.q: What makes it easier to start changing your life?
a: A sense of urgency about your current situation
Waiting until the perfect moment arrives
Reassurance that things will improve on their own
A detailed plan made by someone else
questions.why: Lesson 2 says endings are easier when you feel urgent about leaving your current circumstances.

questions.q: What does the summary suggest doing in front of a mirror?
a: Honestly examine how your current life feels
Rehearse a speech for your boss
Practice smiling through difficult feelings
Repeat affirmations about future success
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends looking at yourself honestly, feeling your present state, then imagining carrying it into the future.

questions.q: Before ending a relationship, what should you do first?
a: State your standards clearly and let the other decide
Announce the breakup without any discussion
List every fault the other person has
Ask friends to deliver the news
questions.why: Lesson 3 says to be clear about your standards, communicate them, and let the other person decide if they can meet them.
